title_en: Wang Deqin v. Yang Desheng and Luzhou City Automobile Second Team — dispute over compensation for traffic accident damages
ruling_gist_en: The 'persons whom the deceased supported during his/her lifetime' as provided in Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC includes not only those actually supported by the deceased during his/her lifetime, but also children who should have been supported by the deceased but whom the deceased had not yet supported due to the fatal accident.
keywords_en: civil; traffic accident compensation dispute; first instance; basic people's court; Sichuan Province; natural person; legal person; General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC; compensation for support of posthumous child; scope of persons supported by deceased during lifetime; favoring plaintiff; traffic accident; posthumous child; paternity test; traffic accident compensation dispute (second category)
full_text_en:
Wang Deqin v. Yang Desheng, Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 — dispute over compensation for damages in a traffic accident

【Ruling Summary】

The "persons whom the deceased supported before his death" as stipulated in Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC includes not only persons actually supported by the deceased during his lifetime, but also children who should have been supported by the deceased but were not yet supported by him due to the fatal accident.

Plaintiff: Wang Deqin, male, 1 year old, residing in Lantian Town, Jiangyang District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Mou Ping, female, 22 years old, mother of the plaintiff Wang Deqin, address same as above.

Defendant: Yang Desheng, male, 39 years old, residing in Mianhuapo Township, Naxi District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Sichuan Province Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2, domiciled at Longmatan District, Luzhou City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Xiao Kaihong, manager of the team.

The plaintiff, Wang Deqin, initiated a lawsuit in the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, Sichuan Province, through his legal representative Mou Ping, against the defendants Yang Desheng and Sichuan Province Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 for compensation for damages arising from a road traffic accident.

The legal representative of the plaintiff Wang Deqin alleged on his behalf: In a traffic accident, the plaintiff's father, Wang Xianqiang, was run over and killed by a vehicle driven by the defendant Yang Desheng, which was affiliated with the defendant Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2. The traffic police department determined that Yang Desheng bore primary responsibility for the traffic accident. Pursuant to Article 119 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of the Civil Law) and Article 28 of the *Law of Succession of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the Law of Succession), the necessary living expenses and education expenses for the plaintiff should be compensated by Yang Desheng, and Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 should bear joint and several liability for compensation. Due to Yang Desheng's objection, this compensation was not resolved in the civil judgment attached to the criminal case of the traffic accident. The plaintiff requested the court to order: (1) the defendants to pay the plaintiff living expenses and education expenses totaling 18,458 yuan; (2) the defendants to pay the plaintiff moral damages of 10,000 yuan; (3) the defendants to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The plaintiff Wang Deqin submitted the following evidence:

1. One Road Traffic Accident Liability Determination No. 2002065, two mediation agreements for compensation for damages in road traffic accidents dated June 8, 2002, and July 1, 2002, one Termination of Mediation for Compensation for Damages in Road Traffic Accidents No. 2002003, one civil judgment attached to the criminal case (2002) Jiangyang Xing Chu Zi No. 234 from the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou, and one civil mediation agreement attached to the criminal case (2002) Lu Xing Zhong Zi No. 101 from the Luzhou Intermediate People's Court, to prove that although Yang Desheng assumed 90% of the liability for compensation in the traffic accident case, this did not include the items claimed by the plaintiff.

2. Two certificates from the Fenghuangshan Agricultural Cooperative, Shangba Village, Lantian Town, Jiangyang District, Luzhou, and two investigation records of witnesses Mao Xihua and Wang Shulin, to prove that Wang Xianqiang and Mou Ping had been in a free love relationship for many years and lived together; Wang Xianqiang died during the process of going through marriage formalities with Mou Ping, at which time Mou Ping was pregnant.

3. One birth medical record and 15 medical invoices, to prove that Mou Ping gave birth to Wang Deqin on October 22, 2002, at the Luzhou Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Sichuan Province, incurring medical expenses of 3,238 yuan.

4. Witness testimonies of Mou Ping, Tang Huali, Deng Jianhua, Gao Xiaohong, and Mou Yong, one forensic identification report 2003-077 from the Sichuan West China Medical Identification Center, and two identification invoices, to prove that Mou Yong extracted a blood sample from Wang Xianqiang's body and handed it to the police for preservation, and that paternity testing confirmed Wang Deqin was indeed the biological son of Wang Xianqiang.

5. One certificate from the Luzhou Civil Affairs Bureau of Sichuan Province, to prove that the local minimum subsistence standard was 130 yuan per person per month.

Defendant Yang Desheng argued: Wang Xianqiang was unmarried at the time of his death and had no spouse, so how could he have a child? Article 9 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "A citizen shall have the capacity for civil rights from birth to death and shall enjoy civil rights and assume civil obligations in accordance with the law." Even if the plaintiff is considered Wang Xianqiang's posthumous child, he was not yet born at the time of Wang Xianqiang's death and was not a civil subject with capacity for civil rights capable of exercising claims. Article 28 of the Law of Succession provides: "When dividing an estate, a share shall be reserved for a posthumous child. If the posthumous child is stillborn, the reserved share shall be dealt with in accordance with statutory succession." This case is a dispute over compensation for damages in a traffic accident, not a succession case. Compensation money is not equivalent to an estate, and the provision on reserving a share for a posthumous child is not applicable to this case. Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Any person who infringes upon a citizen's person and causes injury shall compensate for medical expenses, reduced income for lost working time, living allowances for the disabled, etc.; if death is caused, the person shall also pay funeral expenses, necessary living expenses for persons whom the deceased supported before his death, etc." In the traffic accident case, the issue of economic compensation for persons supported by Wang Xianqiang before his death has already been resolved incidentally. The plaintiff is not a person whom Wang Xianqiang supported before his death and cannot claim compensation under this provision; the plaintiff's claims should be dismissed.

Defendant Yang Desheng submitted a permanent residence registration form from the Lantian Police Station of the Luzhou Public Security Bureau of Sichuan Province, to prove that Wang Xianqiang was unmarried and that he and Mou Ping did not have a marital relationship.

Defendant Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 argued: Even if it could be proven that the plaintiff Wang Deqin was the posthumous child of the victim Wang Xianqiang, compensation should only be made in accordance with the *Measures for the Handling of Road Traffic Accidents*. What moral damage does a one-year-old child understand? Why claim moral damages? The plaintiff's entire claims should not be satisfied.

Defendant Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 did not submit evidence.

The court conducted examination and verification of evidence. The defendants confirmed the authenticity of parts of the evidence submitted by the plaintiff in groups 1, 2, 3, 5, and group 4, but argued that the blood sample was extracted by the plaintiff's relatives without the participation of the traffic police handling the accident, rendering the procedure unlawful and its authenticity questionable, and therefore denied the relevance of other evidence in group 4 to this case. The plaintiff raised no objection to the evidence of Wang Xianqiang's unmarried status submitted by defendant Yang Desheng.

The court held: Most of the evidence submitted by the plaintiff and the evidence submitted by defendant Yang Desheng were confirmed because neither party disputed them. Regarding the blood sample extraction, upon examination, when the traffic police mediated the compensation dispute for the traffic accident, because the child had not yet been born, the traffic police considered that they had no authority to resolve the issue of compensation for a posthumous child and had no need to prove what they had no authority to resolve, so they did not extract Wang Xianqiang's blood sample. However, before Wang Xianqiang's remains were cremated, the handling police officer realized that failure to preserve a blood sample might create difficulties in resolving this issue in the future, so he reminded the deceased's relatives. Mou Yong then publicly collected blood from Wang Xianqiang's body, sealed it, and immediately handed it to the handling police officer for preservation. The extraction of Wang Xianqiang's blood sample by Mou Yong under those specific circumstances was confirmed by multiple witnesses including Tang Huali, Mou Ping, Deng Jianhua, and Gao Xiaohong. Mou Yong's evidence collection was truthful, objective, and did not violate legal provisions; it constituted a valid civil act. The identification based on the blood sample extracted by Mou Yong is relevant to this case and should be admitted.

The Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou found through trial:

On April 27, 2002, defendant Yang Desheng, whose vehicle was affiliated with defendant Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2, drove a small truck (license plate Chuan E07363) from Anfu Town, Naxi District, Luzhou, heading toward Luzhou along the Luzhou-Naxi secondary highway. When the vehicle reached 3KM + 200M of the highway and was passing another vehicle, due to insufficient observation of the road conditions ahead, Yang Desheng struck Wang Xianqiang, who was walking in the same direction driving pigs. Wang Xianqiang died after rescue efforts failed. The Second Brigade of the Luzhou Public Security Bureau Traffic Police Detachment determined that Yang Desheng bore primary responsibility for the accident. When resolving the civil compensation liability that Yang Desheng should bear for the traffic accident, the parents of the victim Wang Xianqiang requested that Yang Desheng and Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 jointly and severally compensate for "child support for the unborn child." Because Wang Xianqiang was unmarried at the time of his death and had no wife, and the child had not yet been born, making it impossible to determine the relationship with Wang Xianqiang, and because Yang Desheng objected, this claim was not satisfied. On October 22, 2002, Mou Ping gave birth to the plaintiff Wang Deqin. In January 2003, Mou Ping, acting as Wang Deqin's representative, filed this lawsuit.

During the trial, upon the application of the plaintiff Wang Deqin, the court ordered the extraction of the blood sample of the victim Wang Xianqiang preserved at the traffic police station and the blood-stained clothing of Wang Xianqiang preserved by his mother, and sent them to the Sichuan West China Forensic Medical Identification Center for identification. Because the blood-stained clothing had deteriorated and lost the conditions for testing, the Center only performed identification on the blood sample. The conclusion was: Wang Xianqiang is the biological father of Wang Deqin.

The court also found: The plaintiff Wang Deqin's mother, Mou Ping, and Wang Xianqiang had been in a free love relationship for many years and lived together. When Wang Xianqiang died, Mou Ping was pregnant. In 2002, the minimum subsistence standard in Luzhou City was 130 yuan per month, and the annual education expenses were approximately 444 yuan.

The focus of the dispute in this case was: Does a tortfeasor bear liability for compensation to a fetus left behind upon the victim's death?

The Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou held:

The evidence in this case proves that there is a father-son blood relationship between the plaintiff Wang Deqin and the victim Wang Xianqiang. Article 21 of the *Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China* provides: "Parents have the duty to bring up and educate their children; children have the duty to support and assist their parents." Article 25 provides: "Children born out of wedlock shall enjoy the same rights as children born in wedlock, and no one may harm or discriminate against them." The duty of parents to bring up and educate their children is determined by the blood relationship between them and does not substantially change depending on whether a marriage relationship exists between the parents.

Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides that where a person infringes upon a citizen's person and causes death, the tortfeasor shall pay to the victim's side necessary living expenses for persons whom the deceased supported before his death. "Persons whom the deceased supported before his death" includes not only persons actually supported by the deceased during his lifetime, but also children who should have been supported by the deceased but were not yet supported by him due to the fatal accident. The plaintiff Wang Deqin has a father-son relationship with Wang Xianqiang and is a person that Wang Xianqiang should have supported. After Wang Deqin was born, his claim for compensation against the person who injured Wang Xianqiang complies with this provision of the General Principles of the Civil Law. Due to the tortious act of defendant Yang Desheng, Wang Xianqiang died before Wang Deqin was born, depriving Wang Deqin of the support from his father Wang Xianqiang. Yang Desheng should compensate for one-half of the necessary expenses such as living expenses and education expenses for Wang Deqin, which should have been borne by Wang Xianqiang. Living expenses are calculated at the Luzhou City 2002 minimum subsistence standard of 130 yuan per month, and education expenses at 444 yuan per year, until Wang Deqin reaches 18 years of age. Article 131 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "If the victim is also at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the civil liability of the injuring party may be reduced." Considering that Wang Xianqiang also had some fault in the traffic accident, Yang Desheng's liability for compensation may be reduced by 10%. Defendant Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 is the entity with which Yang Desheng's vehicle was affiliated and shall bear the liability for advance payment if Yang Desheng is unable to pay the compensation.

The plaintiff Wang Deqin's request for the defendants to pay moral damages was not in accordance with the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's *Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Liability for Compensation for Mental Damage in Civil Torts* and was not supported.

Accordingly, on May 28, 2003, the Jiangyang District People's Court of Luzhou rendered the following judgment:

1. Within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, defendant Yang Desheng shall pay the plaintiff Wang Deqin living expenses of 12,636 yuan and education expenses of 3,600 yuan, totaling 16,236 yuan, in a lump sum; the remaining loss of 1,804 yuan shall be borne by Wang Deqin himself;

2. Defendant Luzhou City Automobile Team No. 2 shall bear the liability for advance payment for the above compensation;

3. The plaintiff Wang Deqin's other claims are dismissed.

Litigation costs of 1,712 yuan and identification fees of 4,000 yuan, totaling 5,712 yuan, shall be borne by the plaintiff Wang Deqin in the amount of 812 yuan and by the defendant Yang Desheng in the amount of 4,900 yuan.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither party appealed. After the judgment took effect, the defendant party voluntarily performed the payment obligations specified in the judgment.
